gaps.sentence: Don't phone between seven and eight — we ___ dinner then.
gaps.hint: in progress at a stated future time
gaps.explanation: Something in progress at a stated future time takes the future continuous: will be having.

gaps.sentence: We ___ to Greece for our honeymoon, but that was twenty years ago.
gaps.hint: twenty years ago fixes a finished past
gaps.explanation: A finished time expression like 'twenty years ago' demands the past simple: went.

gaps.hint: on the point of happening now
gaps.explanation: 'Be about to' expresses something on the point of happening: is about to start.

gaps.sentence: By the time the fire crew arrived, the neighbours ___ the blaze out with buckets of water.
gaps.explanation: The putting out happened before the crew arrived: past perfect 'had put'.

gaps.sentence: She ___ her laptop repaired twice this year already.
gaps.explanation: 'Has had it repaired twice this year' — present perfect of causative have.

gaps.sentence: Every time I visit, she ___ something delicious from the garden.
gaps.hint: every time marks a repeated habit
gaps.explanation: 'Every time' marks a repeated action, which takes the present simple: brings.

gaps.sentence: I ___ that film three times, and I would happily watch it again.
gaps.hint: life experience counted up to now
gaps.explanation: Experience up to the present with no specific past time takes the present perfect: have seen.

gaps.sentence: She is exhausted because she ___ since dawn.
gaps.hint: since dawn explains her present exhaustion
gaps.explanation: An action running from the past to now and explaining a present state takes the present perfect continuous: has been travelling.
